logline: Ex-military bomb disposal officer Lana Washington navigates London's Metropolitan Police bomb squad through a terrorist campaign - a raw procedural that runs on Vicky McClure's magnetic screen presence and genuine tension.

bollymeter.basis: 83% on Rotten Tomatoes from 12 critics; consensus praised Vicky McClure's performance and the show's tense bomb-disposal set-pieces, though plot scrutiny revealed structural weaknesses.

pull_quotes.text: A new and bonkers British police drama - all wailing sirens, explosions and terse dialogue.
What saves the series are the strong performances.

seasons.review_body: Daniel Brierley's bomb disposal thriller launched in January 2022 as ITV's flagship Sunday drama, earning 83% on Rotten Tomatoes from 12 critics on the strength of Vicky McClure's performance as EXPO Lana Washington. The split between critical and audience reception - 83% critic approval versus a 6.3 IMDb score - reflects the show's central tension: McClure elevates material that critics found 'bonkers' and audience members found implausible under close inspection. The six-episode format keeps the pace punishing and the set-pieces visceral, giving the bomb disposal sequences a procedural authenticity that distinguishes it from generic UK crime drama. Season 1 became ITV's most-watched new drama of 2022, demonstrating the show's mainstream grip even if critical consensus was measured.

episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The series opener drops Lana Washington into a London bomb threat scenario with immediate tension - McClure's physicality and focus make the technical procedural feel personal.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first bomb disposal sequence establishes the show's unflinching commitment to practical tension over dramatic shortcuts.

bollymeter.basis: 82% on Rotten Tomatoes from 11 critics; Season 2 sustained the show's formula with a new case and supporting cast while maintaining McClure at the centre.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 returned in January 2024 with a new case, a refreshed supporting cast, and Vicky McClure once again doing the heavy lifting that holds the show together. Critics maintained an 82% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes from 11 reviewers - a steady score that reflects the show's consistency rather than any dramatic evolution. The season formula mirrors the first: six tightly packed episodes, bomb disposal set-pieces that generate genuine suspense, and a plot architecture that rewards pace over scrutiny. Audience IMDb ratings held at 6.3, suggesting the gap between critical appreciation for McClure's craft and audience frustration with narrative convenience remained consistent.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 replicates the formula without transforming it - steady quality, same ceiling, same floor.
